newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - INDIAN NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - INDIAN NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
All papers
135 FEARED DEAD IN FLASH FLOODS
At least 135 people were feared to have been killed in flash floods that hit the northern state of Himachal Pradesh.
The Economic Times
BANK GUARANTEE NO MORE NEEDED UNDER EXPORT SCHEME

The Finance Ministry decided to do away with bank guarantees to get import licences under the Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Scheme. Companies can now obtain this licence by providing corporate guarantees. The guarantees will now be executed by the flagship of the group in favour of group companies. The guarantee will remain in force for the full period plus one year after the expiry of the export obligation period.
COLGATE PALMOLIVE PRUNES DIVIDEND

Colgate Palmolive (India) which is a subsidiary of the U.S. consumer major Colgate Palmolive, pruned the dividend by three percentage points to 45 percent for 1996/97 (April-March) from 48 percent of the previous year. This is the first time in 10 years that the company is pruning its dividend. The reason for the cut is stated to be the fall in profit margins in 1996/97.
Financial Express
BOURSE INDICATOR FALLS BY 57 POINTS

The 30-share Bombay bourse lost 56.27 points to 4,425.03 points. The sensitive index which fell below 4,400 points during the session recovered slightly towards the end. The fall in stock prices was attributed to the bourse regulator putting off a discussion on the modified carry forward system to its next board meeting.
INDEPENDENT POWER PRODUCERS GET REBATE

The Petroleum Ministry decided to give a 15 percent rebate in commitment charges payable by independent power producers (IPPs) to the national oil companies. This rebate will be applicable only for IPPs who use fuel oil for their power plants and have plants situated at ports.
Business Standard
GOLDMAN SACHES, MERRILL AND HSBC GET MTNL MANDATE

Goldman Sachs, HSBC Capital Markets and Merril Lynch were appointed joint global coordinators to a global depositary receipts and share offering by the Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL), the fixed telephone service provider for Delhi and Bombay. Barclays de Zoete Wedd, Morgan Stanley and the Robert Fleming-Jardine Fleming combine bagged the mandate for the Gas Authority of India Ltd's (GAIL) issue. The MTNL offering is expected to raise about $700 million and the GAIL issue about $750 million. Management fees for both the issues together are expected to be $30 million.
HONDA MOTORS AND KINETIC IN DISPUTE OVER TRADEMARK

Japanese auto giant Honda is in a dispute with Kinetic Engineering, its joint venture partner, over trademark rights to the City brand. Honda has written to the Firodias who control Kinetic Engineering not to use the 'City' brand name for their proposed 500 cc car saying it will violate Honda's international trademark right to the brand. Honda plans to launch its City car early next year in India through a joint venture with India's Siel Ltd. Kinetic Engineering has already announced its plans to introduce its own three-door City Car for the domestic passenger segment.
The Observer
FINANCIAL FIRMS TOLD TO SLASH REPRESENTATIVES

The Finance Ministry directed leading financial institutions to reduce the number of nominee directors on the boards of various companies. The ministry is also revising the guidelines for the nominee directors aimed at tightening various norms. It instructed the financial institutions to keep their nominee directors only on the boards of those corporates in which their exposure will exceed a certain percentage of the company's net worth. The percentage of net worth will vary from company to company depending on the risk exposure of the corporates.
INDIAN OIL CORPORATION, PETRONAS SIGN PACT

The Indian Oil corporation and the Petroliam Nasional Berhad (Petronas) of Malaysia signed a joint venture agreement to set up an import and marketing facility for liquefied petroleum gas. The plant, to be set up in Haldia in west Bengal, will be operational by the year 2000. The joint venture to be known as Indian Oil Petronas will have a 50 to 50 equity participation by the promotors.
Business Line
DECISION ON CARRY FORWARD TRADING SYSTEM PUT OFF

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has put off a decision on the modified carry forward trade system as recommended by the Verma Committee. It has also deferred decisions on changes in the guidelines to exclude non-banking finance companies' activities from SEBI's purview and amendments to mutual fund guidelines.
